stories.title: Enhancing El-Shohada distribution network: techno-economic optimization of PV and EV infrastructure using growth optimization algorithm
stories.description: This paper presents a comprehensive techno-economic framework for the optimal integration of distributed energy resources (DERs)—specifically Photovoltaic (PV) solar generation—and Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS) into modern electrical distribution grids. The methodology is applied to a realistic 25-bus, 11 kV radial distribution network modeled after the El-Shohada district in Menofia Governorate, Egypt. To balance inherently conflicting technical and financial objectives, a multi-objective penalty function is formulated. It simultaneously minimizes active power losses, mitigates voltage deviations, and maximizes investor profitability based on contemporary Egyptian energy tariff structures. The recently developed metaheuristic Growth Optimization (GO) algorithm is utilized to determine the optimal bus locations and capacities of these units over a 24-hour horizon, factoring in stochastic load profiles, solar irradiance, and EV charging behavior. Statistical validation based on 30 independent optimization runs demonstrates the high computational efficiency of the GO algorithm, yielding an optimal equilibrium that enhances grid reliability while providing a solid economic foundation.

stories.title: Pentagon funds sponge-based device to treat narrow-entrance battlefield wounds
stories.description:
The US Department of Defense has awarded funding through its APFIT programme to scale production of the XSTAT P15, a hemorrhage control device for narrow-entrance wounds. Developed by the Naval Medical Research Command in partnership with RevMedX, the FDA-cleared applicator uses miniature sponges to control life-threatening bleeding from gunshot or shrapnel wounds.
The device inserts a pouch of sponges that expand and apply pressure within seconds, stopping blood flow without manual compression. The sponges are contained in a mesh bag for easy surgical removal. The technology addresses hemorrhaging, which causes approximately 20% of combat deaths.
The APFIT programme funds small US vendors to transition innovative technologies into operational use. Service members can use the device without additional training, providing a portable life-saving tool in combat environments.
